key_insight: The paper reports the first direct experimental observation of Kelvin-wave turbulence along a single vortex filament, with spectra matching weak-turbulence theory.
engineering_relevance: It provides a validated experimental basis for understanding energy transport along vortex cores, relevant to classical and quantum turbulence modeling.
method: High-resolution spatiotemporal measurements of a single vortex filament
Resolved Kelvin-wave dynamics across a broad range of scales
Compared measured wave-amplitude spectra with weak-turbulence predictions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports wave-amplitude spectra consistent with the predicted weak-turbulence cascade and identifies six-wave resonant interactions as the transfer mechanism.
watch_item: The result is demonstrated under controlled laboratory conditions on a single vortex filament, so direct transfer to more complex turbulent flows may require caution.
paper_title: Experimental evidence of Kelvin wave turbulence along a vortex core
